judgements.reason: OrthogonalL2Bases is declared complete: hermiteHilbertBasis, chebyshevTHilbertBasis and moment determinacy are in Tau Ceti, leaving only packaging. LieHighestWeight still lacks the Weyl character/dimension/Kostant formulas, the Harish-Chandra isomorphism, Serre's presentation theorem and the explicit exceptional Lie algebras.

LieHighestWeight has Layers 0–5 built and needs about three more algebraic layers (Weyl/Kostant formulas, Harish-Chandra and Serre, explicit exceptional algebras). EllipticCurves still needs the dual isogeny, Weil pairing and Tate module, Hasse bound and zeta, the whole local theory (reduction filtration, Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, Tate's algorithm, Tate curve), global minimal models, nonabelian twists and Selmer/Sha with new Galois-cohomology infrastructure, several layers deep.

Neither imports other roadmaps. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra must build depth/Cohen–Macaulay/Auslander–Buchsbaum, Schlessinger, module patching, and a derived layer (perfect complexes, derived completion, Tor spectral sequence, ultrapatching of complexes). EllipticCurves' missing list is broader: dual isogeny, Weil pairing and Tate module, Hasse and zeta, reduction filtration, Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, Tate's algorithm, Tate curve, minimal models/Kraus, twists and Selmer/Sha.

DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra is self-contained commutative and derived algebra with no imports. ProbabilisticAndMetric needs Erdős–Kac, Duffin–Schaeffer, Birkhoff/Gauss-map ergodic theory and multiplicative correlations. It also imports the Weil/Deligne bounds (ES.0 → FF.2 → WC.3, DWP.7, with étale cohomology and Lefschetz pencils) and homogeneous dynamics through GN.0–GN.4.

ZigzagPreprojective needs Koszul duality, Ginzburg/Calabi–Yau completions, Hochschild/A∞ formality and braid actions over the mostly unbuilt DGAInfinity layers, which is large but pure homological algebra. ProbabilisticAndMetric's recorded imports bring Deligne's Weil I/II and the étale cohomology tower (ES.0 → FF.2) plus homogeneous dynamics (GN.4), on top of its own Duffin–Schaeffer and ergodic targets.

Zigzag's remaining theory is homological algebra over the DGAInfinity sibling (A∞ transfer, Hochschild cohomology, Calabi–Yau completions). K3BlochGroups must first build Quillen K-theory (plus construction, Q-construction, homotopy fibres), K₂ symbols and Suslin's exact sequence. V.5–V.6 also import the norm-residue theorem with motivic cohomology (M.1–M.7) and Borel's stable cohomology (N.5, R.1–R.3).

Metaplectic needs nine stacked layers (Stone–von Neumann up to the genus-two cover) plus about 22 imported stages (smooth representations, reduction theory, automorphic forms, Eisenstein continuation). K3BlochGroups imports about 84 stages: Quillen K-theory and homotopy foundations, the norm-residue theorem and motivic cohomology, Borel's theorem and Poitou–Tate. On that base it builds Suslin's sequence and K₃(ℤ) ≅ ℤ/48.

Metaplectic is deeper: a nine-layer chain on top of reduction theory and Langlands' Eisenstein continuation (AS.1–AS.2). OptimalTransport has more missing theory in total: convex duality and Brenier, Caffarelli/MTW/partial regularity, Riemannian McCann with the unbuilt exponential map and curvature, AGS flows and JKO, entropic transport, CD/RCD and Gromov–Wasserstein, plus Schauder and heat-semigroup theory from PDE.

OptimalTransport's remaining layers are vast, but they sit on Mathlib's measure theory and analysis and import only Riemannian geometry and elliptic regularity. AutomorphicBundles needs about 93 imported stages, none in the library: Shimura varieties with canonical models and CM theory, toroidal and minimal compactifications with Faltings–Chai degenerations, PEL/Hilbert moduli, algebraic stacks and characteristic-zero resolution.

Both sit on large unbuilt arithmetic geometry. AutomorphicBundles imports Shimura varieties, canonical models, compactifications, PEL moduli and resolution of singularities (about 93 stages). Lefschetz imports the étale six-functor formalism with perverse sheaves, Deligne's Weil I and II, and for LPV.6 diamond étale cohomology with perfectoid and prismatic comparisons (about 136 stages), which tips the balance.

GL2's import closure contains all of Lefschetz's except LPV.6–LPV.7: the geometric fundamental lemma (decomposition theorem) and local Langlands for GL_n (Shimura-variety cohomology) both pull in Weil II and LPV.0–LPV.5. On top of that GL2 needs smooth representations, Godement–Jacquet/Rankin–Selberg, the invariant trace formula, Jacquet–Langlands, base change and Langlands–Tunnell.

Habiro's extra theory is the K-theory side: Quillen K-theory, Suslin's theorem, the norm-residue theorem, Borel regulators, local K₃ and p-adic regulators, plus Habiro rings (about 104 stages GL2 lacks). GL2's extra theory is about twice that: the étale cohomology and Weil I/II tower, diamond étale cohomology, Shimura varieties, the trace formula, the fundamental lemma and local Langlands for GL_n, besides its own transfer theorems.

Habiro builds K₃-indexed modules on the K-theory, norm-residue and p-adic-regulator tower (closure about 140 stages). ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions must supply potential automorphy over CM fields using all of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure (Igusa varieties, perfectoid Shimura varieties, derived patching, GL_n Galois representations), then Newton–Thorne symmetric powers and Arthur's classification. With PA its closure is about 400 stages.

PadicHodgeRegulators has the larger recorded closure: the K-theory/norm-residue tower, (φ,Γ)-modules and Perrin-Riou/LLZ regulators, and through L4 the GL₂ Galois representations with local–global compatibility at p. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions shares most of the automorphic and étale base and adds, via PA, Igusa varieties, perfectoid Shimura varieties, derived patching and GL_n Galois representations over CM fields. It also needs Newton–Thorne and Arthur's classification, whose stabilization inputs are not even recorded.

Habiro's closure is almost inside PadicHodgeRegulators': only HB.1–HB.7 and HabiroCyclotomicCompletions fall outside. PadicHodgeRegulators adds about 320 stages: (φ,Γ)-modules, Perrin-Riou's big logarithm, LLZ maps, syntomic regulators of curves, and through L4 the GL₂ Galois representations, Shimura varieties and étale/Weil II theory.

EllipticCurves' remaining theory is classical (dual isogeny, Weil pairing, Hasse, Tate's algorithm, Tate curve, Selmer/Sha), with no imports and Mordell–Weil already built. K3BlochGroups needs higher algebraic K-theory from scratch (plus construction, Q-construction, Suslin's exact sequence), and its K₃(ℤ) targets import the norm-residue theorem, motivic cohomology and Borel's stable cohomology.

PadicHodgeRegulators' closure contains all of AutomorphicBundles' imports except the general-data interfaces (V7, C2/C3.general) and B3–B5. It adds about 370 stages: étale cohomology with Weil I/II, GL₂ transfer and Galois representations, the K-theory/norm-residue tower, (φ,Γ)-modules and the Perrin-Riou/LLZ regulators.

OptimalTransport's missing theory is analysis and geometry (Brenier, Monge–Ampère regularity, AGS/JKO, RCD, Gromov–Wasserstein) with modest imports. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions needs potential automorphy over CM fields on top of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure's roughly 380-stage closure (Shimura varieties, Weil II, perfectoid and Igusa geometry, patching), plus Newton–Thorne and Arthur's classification.

LieHighestWeight is mostly built and needs about three algebraic layers (Weyl/Kostant formulas, Harish-Chandra and Serre, exceptional algebras). ProbabilisticAndMetric needs Erdős–Kac, equidistribution and discrepancy, Duffin–Schaeffer, ergodic continued-fraction theory and correlation theorems, and imports the Weil/Deligne bounds and homogeneous dynamics.

Metaplectic's roughly 31-stage closure (smooth representations, reduction theory, automorphic forms, Eisenstein continuation, then MP.0–MP.8) lies inside GL2's except for MP.0–MP.8 themselves. GL2 adds about 230 stages: the full trace formula, transfer factors and the geometric fundamental lemma, local Langlands for GL_n with Shimura varieties and étale/Weil II cohomology, and its own Jacquet–Langlands and base-change theorems.

Zigzag's remaining theory (Koszul duality, Ginzburg DG algebras, Hochschild/A∞ formality, braid actions, over the DGAInfinity layers) is homological algebra. Lefschetz needs the absent étale six-functor formalism and perverse sheaves, Deligne's Weil I/II, nearby cycles, Lefschetz pencils and monodromy, and diamond/perfectoid comparisons for LPV.6.

DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra is nine layers of self-contained commutative and derived algebra with no imports. AutomorphicBundles must first import Shimura data and varieties with canonical models, toroidal compactifications, abelian-scheme and PEL moduli, stacks and resolution of singularities before any automorphic bundle can be defined.

PadicHodgeRegulators' closure contains all of Lefschetz's except LPV.6–LPV.7. It adds about 320 stages: the K-theory/norm-residue tower, GL₂ transfer and modular Galois representations, (φ,Γ)-modules, Iwasawa cohomology and the Perrin-Riou/LLZ regulators.

EllipticCurves' missing theory is classical and self-contained (dual isogeny, Weil pairing, Hasse, local reduction theory, Tate curve, Selmer/Sha). ProbabilisticAndMetric needs Duffin–Schaeffer, pointwise ergodic and continued-fraction theory and multiplicative correlations, and imports Deligne's Weil I/II through ES.0 → FF.2 and homogeneous dynamics through GN.0–GN.4.

K3BlochGroups sits on Quillen K-theory, the norm-residue theorem and Borel's theorem (about 90 stages). ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions, with the PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure it assembles, reaches about 400 stages of automorphic, étale, perfectoid and patching theory. Its endpoints (potential automorphy, symmetric powers, Arthur's classification) are among the deepest known results.
